title: pricing-packaging-scratchpad-v8
body:
Context / goal:
- Quick back-of-envelope for hosted API unit economics + starter tier ideas. Want to validate: 1) per-token price bands vs compute cost, 2) simple starter plan that converts to usage, 3) committed/dedicated pricing anchor.

Assumptions (rough):
- Core infra GPU hourly costs (examples):
  - Reserved/Committed A100-ish baseline: $2.50 / hour
  - On-demand / mixed infra: $3.50 / hour
- Model throughput (tokens/sec per GPU, avg generation workload):
  - 7B-ish model: 200 tok/s
  - 13B-ish: 100 tok/s
  - 70B-ish: 25 tok/s
- Ops & infra overhead (network, control plane, autoscaler, SRE, monitoring, storage): assume additional 2x compute cost baseline (very rough).
- Target gross margin for hosted API initial pricing: ~60-70% (we can iterate).

Raw compute cost math (on-demand $3.50/hr):
- 7B: 200 tok/s -> 720,000 tok/hr -> compute cost = 3.5 / 720k = $0.00000486/token -> $0.00486 per 1k tokens
- 13B: 100 tok/s -> 360,000 tok/hr -> 3.5 / 360k = $0.00000972/token -> $0.00972 per 1k tokens
- 70B: 25 tok/s -> 90,000 tok/hr -> 3.5 / 90k = $0.00003889/token -> $0.03889 per 1k tokens

Add infra+ops overhead (x2): effective cost -> multiply per-1k by 2:
- 7B effective cost per 1k = $0.0097
- 13B effective cost per 1k = $0.0194
- 70B effective cost per 1k = $0.0778

Target retail (apply margin): assume retail = effective_cost * markup where markup ~ 3.0 (gives ~66% margin)
- 7B retail per 1k = $0.0097 * 3 = $0.029 ~ $0.03 per 1k
- 13B retail per 1k = $0.0194 * 3 = $0.0582 ~ $0.06 per 1k
- 70B retail per 1k = $0.0778 * 3 = $0.2334 ~ $0.23 per 1k

Quick sanity check vs market: these are in the ballpark for our positioning (developer-first, performance). We can also tier models/prices (fast/cheap vs high-quality expensive).

Suggested hosted API price bands (initial):
- "fast" 7B tier: $0.03 / 1k tokens (good for chat assistants with short-turn gen)
- "balanced" 13B tier: $0.06 / 1k tokens (default recommendation)
- "high-quality" 70B tier: $0.24 / 1k tokens (large context / complex reasoning)
Notes: We might want to round to prettier numbers: $0.03, $0.06, $0.24. Also consider per-token rather than per-1k unit for docs (easier for devs): 13B -> $0.00006/token.

Starter packs / PLG-friendly offers (examples):
- Free: 2M tokens / month across any model (burstable, fair-use throttling)
- Starter $20/mo: includes 1M tokens (balanced default) THEN overage at PAYG rates (eg $0.06/1k). The aim: low $ barrier to experiment.
- Growth PAYG: no monthly commitment; default PAYG listed above with volume tiers:
   - 0-5M tokens/month: base price
   - 5-50M tokens/month: 10% discount
   - 50-500M tokens/month: 25% discount
- Enterprise committed: custom SLAs + committed usage price (e.g., 30-60% off PAYG depending on commit + reserved capacity offers)

Dedicated / Reserved capacity anchor (example):
- Offer Dedicated GPU pools (managed) priced as: base infra hourly + management fee + network egress. Example anchor: $2.50/hr reserved A100 + $10k/mo management/ops surcharge depending on config.
- Simpler SKU: 1 GPU reserved = $2,500 / month (this bundles $1,800 compute + $700 management/overhead).
   - If customer wants 3 GPUs reserved: $7,000 / month (tiered discount applies).
- Convert reserved to token economics for customers who want price-per-output: we can estimate tokens/hr per reserved GPU and give an effective price per 1k tokens (use throughput numbers).

Embeddings pricing (notes):
- Embedding compute is cheaper but memory bound. Example: $0.005 per 1k embeddings (placeholder) or $0.0004 per vector (if representing per-vector). Need infra numbers from infra team.

Other levers / experiments:
- Batching & caching: enable higher effective throughput -> lowers compute cost per token. We should model scenarios where batching improves throughput by 1.5x-3x for typical workloads.
- Quantized model variants: offer cheap/fast quantized SKU (e.g., 7B-quant) at 50% of standard price.
- Hybrid routing: route to cheaper model for low-importance requests. Could offer bundled routed pricing.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Get real infra cost numbers from infra/finance: per-GPU reserved vs on-demand across cloud partners. (JIRA: JIRA-PRICING-56)
- Measure real throughput for our model builds (7B/13B/70B) under typical request mix + prefix caching. Add numbers here and re-run calcs. (TODO: bench script: github PR referenced above).
- Decide free tokens threshold (2M might be too high/low). A/B test 500k vs 2M vs 5M.
- Decide how to present pricing in console: per-1k tokens + model selector + effective per-request estimate.
- Confirm embedding SKU units (per-vector vs per-1k vectors).

Quick scenarios (customer examples):
- Small startup: 100k tokens/day (3M tokens/mo) on 13B -> retail cost @ $0.06/1k = $180 / month. If we offer Starter $20/mo with 1M included + overage: they pay $20 + 2M overage* $0.06/1k = $120 -> $140/mo. Starter seems reasonable conversion path.
- Mid-market team: 20M tokens/mo (13B) -> PAYG $0.06 * 20k = $1,200/mo. Offer committed 6-12mo 30% off -> $840/mo.

Notes to self (messy):
- Keep simple tiers for marketing; hide complexity in console and show effective per-request cost.
- Need to coordinate with sales for Dedicated packaging: simple anchors, add-ons (support, retention, audit logs).

Bottom line / ask:
- Validate these ballpark retail numbers with infra + finance. If they check out, propose initial public pricing: 7B $0.03/1k, 13B $0.06/1k, 70B $0.24/1k plus embeddings TBD.
- Plan A: launch Starter $20/mo + free credits + usage billing.
- Plan B: experiments (free tokens variations + quantized SKU).

-- end scratchpad --
